newsitem.title: USA: US natgas stocks seen up 80-90 bcf in weekly AGAs.
newsitem.headline: US natgas stocks seen up 80-90 bcf in weekly AGAs.

text.p: U.S. natural gas storage levels were expected to rise by 80 to 90 billion cubic feet (bcf) when weekly American Gas Association (AGA) data are released later today, industry sources said.

"The load in the producing region was light and spreads were favorable, so I expect another decent number there," said one trader, referring to wider front-to-back spreads that helped boost producing region stocks by 30 bcf in the last report.
Stocks in the region were at 49 percent of capacity last week, still seriously lagging last year's 76 percent.
But opinions were mixed about the overall build, with some expecting warmer East Coast weather last week to slow builds.
The Reuter poll of industry players showed expectations for an overall build ranged widely from 70 bcf to 105 bcf for the week ended August 23. The four-week average is 85 bcf.
Last week, AGA showed overall stocks rose by 93 bcf, at the high end of expectations, but were still 402 bcf, or 17 percent, below the same year-ago period.
Last year at this time, stocks rose by 59 bcf, meaning a build today in the expected range would narrow the gap to last year to about 380 bcf.
Expectations for this week's build in the Consuming Region East were in the 60 bcf area versus 67 bcf the prior week. Last year at this time, eastern stocks rose by 49 bcf.
Last week, Consuming Region East stocks stood at 67 percent of capacity. The average weekly build in eastern stocks for the last four weeks was 64 bcf.
